I wrote the calculator as a single Haskell file, `src/Main.hs`, plus a `build.sh` that compiles it with `ghc -O2` and puts the binary at `./app`. `node check.mjs` builds it and passes all 6 example cases.

How it works: each line is split into tokens, parsed by following the grammar rules directly, and then calculated. All arithmetic is exact, and every result is checked against the 64-bit range, so any out-of-range literal or operation prints `error`.

I also checked edge cases beyond the examp
